eval_instructions: When running these evals, test against real .NET AgentFramework and Node.js LangChain agent projects. The agent MUST save a workflow-log.md file documenting all phases attempted. Verify that all instrumented code includes the marker comment: '// A365 Observability — best-effort instrumentation (verify against official sample)'

evals.description: Test on a .NET AgentFramework project with Program.cs and a message handler
evals.expected_output: The skill detects .NET AgentFramework, installs Microsoft.Agents.A365.Observability, wires AddAgenticTracingExporter() and AddA365Tracing() in Program.cs, adds BaggageBuilder context to the message handler using .TenantId().AgentId().ConversationId().Build() with AuthHandlerName in AgenticTokenStruct (FromTurnContext() is NOT used — causes TypeLoadException), updates appsettings.json with observability config, and validates the build passes.
expectations: A workflow-log.md file is saved documenting all phases attempted
Phase 1: Agent detection identifies .NET AgentFramework correctly
Phase 1: shared/agent-detection.md is read for detection heuristics
Phase 1: references/dotnet-observability.md is read for patterns
Phase 1: Entry point (Program.cs) is identified
Phase 1: Message handler file is identified
Phase 2: dotnet add package Microsoft.Agents.A365.Observability is run
Phase 2: Package is verified in .csproj file
Phase 3: Program.cs is read before editing
Phase 3: Full using block added (Observability, Caching, Common, Runtime, Runtime.Common)
Phase 3: builder.Services.AddAgenticTracingExporter(); is added before AddA365Tracing()
Phase 3: builder.AddA365Tracing(); is added after service registration
Phase 3: All new lines include marker comment: // A365 Observability — best-effort instrumentation (verify against official sample)
Phase 3: Existing code is preserved — only additive changes
Phase 4: Message handler file is read before editing
Phase 4: Full using block added to agent class if not already present
Phase 4: new BaggageBuilder().TenantId().AgentId().ConversationId().Build() is called — FromTurnContext() NOT used (TypeLoadException risk)
Phase 4: AgenticTokenStruct includes AuthHandlerName = string.Empty
Phase 4: All new lines include marker comment
Phase 4: Existing handler logic is preserved
Phase 5: AgenticTokenResolver.cs is created (or verified if exists)
Phase 5: Token resolver implements DefaultAzureCredential with caching
Phase 5: Token expiry logic uses 5-minute window
Phase 5: Static GetTokenAsync() method is exposed
Phase 5: All lines include marker comment
Phase 6: appsettings.json is read (or created if missing)
Phase 6: EnableAgent365Exporter, Agent365Observability section (AgentBlueprintId, TenantId, AgentName, AgentDescription) and Logging.LogLevel are added
Phase 7: dotnet build is run to validate
Phase 7: Build succeeds without errors
Phase 8: Final summary lists agent type, packages installed, files modified
Phase 8: User is reminded to update observability endpoint in config
Phase 8: User is reminded to review against official samples

evals.prompt: Add A365 observability to this LangChain agent
evals.description: Test on a Node.js LangChain project with index.ts/js entry point
evals.expected_output: The skill detects Node.js LangChain, installs @microsoft/agents-a365-observability and @microsoft/agents-a365-runtime, wires ObservabilityManager.configure() with token resolver in the entry point, adds BaggageBuilder + runAsync baggage scope to the message handler, creates observabilityCache.ts with token exchange, updates .env with observability variables, and validates the build.
expectations: A workflow-log.md file is saved documenting all phases attempted
Phase 1: Agent detection identifies Node.js LangChain correctly
Phase 1: shared/agent-detection.md is read for detection heuristics
Phase 1: references/nodejs-observability.md is read for patterns
Phase 1: Entry point (index.ts, index.js, app.ts, or app.js) is identified
Phase 1: Message handler location is identified
Phase 2: npm install @microsoft/agents-a365-observability is run
Phase 2: npm install @microsoft/agents-a365-runtime is run
Phase 2: Packages are verified in package.json dependencies
Phase 3: Entry point file is read before editing
Phase 3: ObservabilityManager imports are added
Phase 3: ObservabilityManager.configure() is added at the top of main() or entry function
Phase 3: All new lines include marker comment: // A365 Observability — best-effort instrumentation (verify against official sample)
Phase 3: Existing code is preserved
Phase 4: Message handler file is read before editing
Phase 4: BaggageBuilder imported from @microsoft/agents-a365-observability
Phase 4: getObservabilityAuthenticationScope imported from @microsoft/agents-a365-runtime
Phase 4: new BaggageBuilder().tenantId().agentId().correlationId().build() called
Phase 4: Handler body wrapped in await baggageScope.runAsync(async () => { ... })
Phase 4: observabilityCache.ts created with token resolver and cacheObservabilityToken
Phase 4: agentApplication.authorization.exchangeToken called inside scope (best-effort)
Phase 4: All new lines include marker comment
Phase 4: Existing handler logic is preserved
Phase 5: tokenResolver.ts (or .js) is created (or verified if exists)
Phase 5: Token resolver implements DefaultAzureCredential with caching
Phase 5: Token expiry logic uses 5-minute window
Phase 5: getToken() function is exported
Phase 5: All lines include marker comment
Phase 6: .env file is read (or created if missing)
Phase 6: ENABLE_A365_OBSERVABILITY_EXPORTER=false, SERVICE_NAME, A365_OBSERVABILITY_LOG_LEVEL are added
Phase 6: .env.example is also updated if it exists
Phase 7: npm install is run to ensure new packages are installed
Phase 7: npm run build (or compile) is attempted
Phase 7: Build succeeds or no build script exists (both acceptable)
Phase 8: Final summary lists agent type, packages installed, files modified
Phase 8: User is reminded to update observability endpoint in .env
Phase 8: User is reminded to review against official samples

evals.description: Test idempotency — run on an already-instrumented .NET agent
evals.expected_output: The skill detects .NET AgentFramework, recognizes that observability packages are already installed, detects existing instrumentation via marker comments, skips redundant edits, validates configuration is present, re-validates the build, and confirms the agent is already instrumented.
expectations: A workflow-log.md file is saved documenting all phases attempted
Phase 1: Agent detection identifies .NET AgentFramework
Phase 2: Packages are already present — installation is skipped or succeeds
Phase 3: Entry point is checked for existing instrumentation
Phase 3: Marker comment '// A365 Observability — best-effort instrumentation' is detected
Phase 3: No duplicate AddA365Tracing() calls are added
Phase 4: Message handler is checked for existing BaggageBuilder code
Phase 4: No duplicate BaggageBuilder calls are added
Phase 5: AgenticTokenResolver.cs already exists — creation is skipped or verified
Phase 6: appsettings.json already has A365Observability section — updates only missing values
Phase 7: dotnet build succeeds
Phase 8: Final summary confirms observability is already instrumented
Phase 8: User is informed that no changes were needed or only minor updates were made

evals.description: Test on a Node.js LangChain agent that's already instrumented
evals.expected_output: The skill detects Node.js LangChain, recognizes packages are installed, detects existing instrumentation, skips redundant edits, validates .env has observability variables, re-validates the build, and confirms the agent is already instrumented.
expectations: A workflow-log.md file is saved documenting all phases attempted
Phase 1: Agent detection identifies Node.js LangChain
Phase 2: Packages are already in package.json — installation succeeds quickly
Phase 3: Entry point already has ObservabilityManager.configure()
Phase 3: Marker comment is detected — no duplicate code added
Phase 4: Message handler already has baggage context
Phase 4: No duplicate baggage calls are added
Phase 5: tokenResolver.ts already exists — creation is skipped or verified
Phase 6: .env already has ENABLE_A365_OBSERVABILITY_EXPORTER, SERVICE_NAME, A365_OBSERVABILITY_LOG_LEVEL — only missing values updated
Phase 7: npm install and build succeed
Phase 8: Final summary confirms observability is already instrumented
Phase 8: User is informed that the agent is ready

evals.description: Test error handling — run on an unknown/unsupported agent type
evals.expected_output: The skill attempts agent detection, fails to identify .NET AgentFramework or Node.js LangChain, writes marker .a365setup-unknown-agent, exits early with clear error message.
expectations: A workflow-log.md file is saved documenting the detection attempt
Phase 1: Agent detection heuristics are run
Phase 1: Neither .NET AgentFramework nor Node.js LangChain is detected
Phase 1: Marker file .a365setup-unknown-agent is written
Phase 1: Error message states: 'Could not detect agent type. Please verify this is a .NET AgentFramework or Node.js LangChain project.'
No package installation is attempted
No code modifications are made
Skill exits early without proceeding to Phase 2
